Cannot reproduce a crash with this code on 4.4 stable and 4.5 dev 2, is there something else going on in the project?

System info: Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.13031.3015) - AMD Ryzen 9 5900XT 16-Core Processor (32 threads)

Thanks for the reply.
I just tested it on another machine and didn‘t experience any crashes either. Here‘s the information from my other machine: ’Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono -Windows 11 24H2 Vulkan(Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6750 GRE 10GB‘. 
I may need to test it on the previous machine using version 4.4.1 and conduct additional tests on other machines to determine whether the issue is related to the software version or specific to my machine.

I was unable to reproduce the issue. My PC uses an AMD GPU and the other two tests that didn't crashed also use an AMD GPU so maybe a Nvidia specific issue?

Godot v4.4.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 580 2048SP (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 31.0.21921.1000) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor (12 threads)

> I was unable to reproduce the issue. My PC uses an AMD GPU and the other two tests that didn't crashed also use an AMD GPU so maybe a Nvidia specific issue?

Thank you for your reply! 
I just tested the Godot 4.4.1 version on my Nvidia 4060 GPU machine, and it still crashes. I also asked two friends to help me test, and the program crashes on their machines as well. Their computer information is 'Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono  - Windows11 23H2
Vulkan(Forward+) NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060' and 'Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - Windows10 22H2
Vulkan(Forward+) NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070'. 
The current situation is that the program crashes on machines with Nvidia GPUs, but not on machines with AMD GPUs. 
I hope someone can help me resolve this issue.

I can reproduce it on an RTX 3070.

> I can reproduce it on an RTX 3070.
> 
> Chash with an `Unhandled exception at 0x00007FFFC521451B (nvoglv64.dll) in godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.exe: 0xC0000094: Integer division by zero.`
> 
Thank you for your reply! 
It seems that Godot's RenderingDevice class does not have good support for Nvidia GPUs.

Its very likely you are requesting a type of memory that your GPU does not support and thus Vulkan is failing to allocate the space for the texture. 

That being said, if that is the case, it is a bug that Godot crashes, we should return an error message without crashing in such a case.

> Its very likely you are requesting a type of memory that your GPU does not support and thus Vulkan is failing to allocate the space for the texture.
> 
Thank you for your reply! Could you please provide more specific details? Does the unsupported type refer to ‘format’ or ‘usage_bits’?
Search for `R8G8B8_SRGB` here https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/listlineartilingformats.php. It has no support on the majority of devices.

> Search for `R8G8B8_SRGB` here https://vulkan.gpuinfo.org/listlineartilingformats.php. It has no support on the majority of devices.

Thank you for your reply!
I was indeed able to create textures successfully after changing to the R8G8B8A8_UINT format.

I guess the documentation should point to [`texture_is_format_supported_for_usage`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_renderingdevice.html#class-renderingdevice-method-texture-is-format-supported-for-usage) more frequently so that users are aware of the need to whether formats are supported.
